reason: The messenger cell’s empty display suggests it first needs a bacterial fragment to initiate the immune response.
expectation: The messenger cell will capture bacterial material and display a fragment.

effect: The messenger displays a bacterial fragment and travels to a lymph node, suggesting it can now meet a matching helper T cell there.
reaction: The link between the airway encounter and the lymph node is clear.
reason: The helper T cells include one that matches the displayed fragment.
expectation: The matching helper T cell will recognize the displayed fragment and become activated.

effect: The matching helper T cells activate at the lymph node, where the messenger presents the bacterial fragment.
reaction: The location requirement was a little surprising, but the result makes the interaction clear.
reason: One B cell matches the intact bacterial surface protein, so I’ll try bringing them together.
expectation: The matching B cell will recognize the bacteria, preparing it to respond.

effect: The matching B cell binds the bacterial protein and displays a fragment, suggesting it can interact with the activated helper T cells.
reaction: The different roles of the intact protein and displayed fragment are becoming clearer.
reason: The activated helper T cells may help the B cell respond at the lymph node.
expectation: The B cell and activated helper T cells will interact at the node, activating the matching B cell.

effect: The matching helper T cell has signaled the B cell at the lymph node, so the helped B cells are the next likely step toward antibodies and memory.
reaction: The two-cell interaction makes their different roles clearer.
reason: I’ll inspect the helped B cells to find how they can produce antibodies or memory cells.
expectation: The report will show the available next step for the helped B cells.

effect: The helped B cells multiplied at the lymph node into antibody-making plasma cells and memory B cells. The remaining goal is to mark the bacteria and leave the body with memory.
reaction: The branching into two cell roles makes the outcome clear.
reason: The antibody-making cells should be able to target the matching airway bacteria.
expectation: Antibodies will bind to and mark the matching bacteria.

effect: The antibodies tagged matching bacteria, completing the first goal; the body still needs immune memory.
reaction: The reminder that tagging does not eliminate every bacterium makes the result clearer.
reason: The body needs the memory cells produced in the lymph node, so I’ll try connecting it to them.
expectation: The body will retain memory B cells after the encounter.

effect: The body retained memory B cells, completing the remaining goal. The result explains that a later response can be faster without guaranteeing complete protection.
reaction: The distinction between immune memory and conscious memory was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: The helped B cells dividing into antibody-making and memory cells made the two outcomes of the response clear and connected the two goals.

leastWorthwhile.text: The lymph node location was not obvious when I first tried to combine the messenger and helper T cells, although the compatibility feedback let the interaction proceed.

surprise.text: The B cell bound the intact bacterial protein and then displayed a fragment, giving the helper T cell a way to contribute to its response.

arbitrary.text: The required lymph node location initially felt somewhat arbitrary; the result showed where the interaction occurred, though it did not explain why it needed to happen there.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: tracing how specific recognition leads to both antibodies and memory was interesting, and the results explained the limits of those defenses.
